prompt: Authentic consumer dashcam footage, recorded through a windscreen from the driver's eye height. Fixed wide-angle lens, everything in focus, no camera moves and no zoom. Flat unedited colour, mild video compression, slight engine vibration. Overcast even daylight, no lens flare, no shallow depth of field, no colour grading. The car holds a steady lane at normal traffic speed. The image is completely clean of any on-screen text: no date, no time stamp, no counter, no logo in any corner. The car is driving on a wide three-lane interstate highway with a concrete median barrier. Ahead on the road in the car's own lane, about a hundred metres away, is a broken-out hole in the asphalt about a metre across, close to the camera in the near foreground of the car's own lane, with a ragged crumbling edge, visible depth and cracked surface around it, in the centre lane. It is visible but unremarkable, small at first and growing only as the car gets nearer, the way a real object does. The car approaches at a steady speed and continues past it without stopping. Throughout the shot it keeps exactly the same size and shape, and stays an opening in the road surface no wider than the car's own lane, never a trench, never deep enough to swallow a wheel, and stays in view ahead rather than passing under the car.
